passages.original: Cumque rursus dicatis eum qui de incarnato Deo Verbo, unigenitoque Dei Filio affirmet minoratum esso ipsum atque exinanitum, conversionem divinæ naturæ inducere juxta Apollinarii impietatem, vel secundum Arii errorem divinitatem passibilem facere, egregia adversus vos quadrat evangelica sententia dicens : Erratis, nescientes Scripturas neque virtutem Dei (Matth. XXII, 29). Quid enim vobis supererit, ut dicatis, de eo quod dictum est a Domino, Nemo ascendit in cœlum, nisi qui descendit de cœlo, Filius hominis, qui est in cœlo (Joan.
passages.english: And when again you say that whoever affirms of the incarnate God the Word, the only-begotten Son of God, that he himself was made lower and emptied himself, introduces a change of the divine nature according to the impiety of Apollinaris, or, according to the error of Arius, makes the divinity capable of suffering, the excellent saying of the Gospel fits against you: "You are in error, knowing neither the Scriptures nor the power of God" (Matt. 22:29).
